exposure: borderline hyperglycemia (abnormal one-hour 50-gram glucose challenge test (GCT) and normal 100-gram oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT))
impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) or gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosed with 100-gram OGTT
outcome: rate of cesarean section delivery in previous pregnancy
duration of hospitalization period for neonates
cohort: Pregnant women categorized into three groups based on their glucose tolerance test results: normal 50-gram GCT (198 cases), abnormal 50-gram GCT with normal 100-gram OGTT (160 cases), and IGT/GDM diagnosed with 100-gram OGTT (212 cases).
finding: Borderline hyperglycemia was associated with longer maternal hospitalization, lower postoperative hemoglobin values, neonatal hypoglycemia, lower first-minute Apgar scores, and longer neonatal hospitalization compared to the normal glucose group, indicating various maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section delivery in previous pregnancy was significantly higher in the IGT/GDM group compared to both the normal and borderline hyperglycemia groups.
